title: Last-coordinate Gowers Cauchy–Schwarz inequality
statement: Let $F$ assign a real-valued function on $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ to each $s\in\mathbb{F}_2^{k+1}$. Its Gowers inner product is at most the product of the square roots of the Gowers inner products of the two families obtained by replacing the last coordinate of every index by $0$ and by $1$, respectively.
hypotheses_covered: A real-valued family $F$ indexed by $\mathbb{F}_2^{k+1}$ and points of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$
